mechanism: README.md 'From Sources' setup instructions describe a browsable Angular single-page web application served via npm start at http://localhost:3000
notes: Establishes the Web UI Functional surface prior to source verification; supports presence CONFIRMED for web in audit.md section 2.

mechanism: Static seed-data file defining a fixed set of named accounts with deterministic email/password pairs (for example email admin, password admin123; also named accounts jim, bender, chris, amy, support, mc.safesearch, and an accounting-role account), each with deterministic role/profile fields
expected_behavior: Logging into the Web UI with a listed account's exact credentials reaches the application in that account's known role/state every time the evaluated version is run, because the account set is redefined identically on every application start (see SUT05-EV-0003)
notes: Deterministic-test-account mechanism, protocol/capability-rubric-v1.md Score 3 example.

mechanism: server.ts calls sequelize.sync with force true on every application start (also seq.sync with force true at line 806), which drops and recreates all database tables, followed by the data creator (data/datacreator.ts) that reloads data/static/*.yml
expected_behavior: Restarting the evaluated application from a fresh process always reproduces the identical initial user/product/basket state defined in the evaluated version's static seed files; no in-session HTTP reset endpoint was found (see SUT05-EV-0028 and limitations.md)
notes: Confirms SUT05-EV-0002's accounts are reproducible from the evaluated version itself, not external tooling. Also supports Resetability (cross-cutting).

mechanism: Injects AdministrationService and defines an isAccounting() role check (line 305) that gates which navigation UI elements are rendered by the logged-in account's role
expected_behavior: Logging in as the admin/accounting accounts named in SUT05-EV-0002 deterministically changes which navigation items (e.g. Administration) are rendered, giving Web UI Functional testing a defined, observable expected outcome tied to a known account
notes: Confirms the defined-expected-outcome half of the Score 3 decision-procedure question for Web UI Functional.

mechanism: OpenAPI 3.0 document describing a versioned NextGen B2B API at /b2b/v2 with a createCustomerOrder operation, request/response JSON schemas, and bearer-JWT security
notes: Establishes the API surface and its documented schema prior to source verification; supports presence CONFIRMED for api in audit.md section 2.

mechanism: POST /rest/user/login accepts the same deterministic accounts as SUT05-EV-0002 and issues a JWT scoped to that account; the same handler runs challengeUtils.solveIf() checks asserting the exact submitted email/password against each named account
expected_behavior: Authenticating via the API with a known account from SUT05-EV-0002 deterministically returns a JWT bound to that account's id/role, usable to seed further API-level state (basket, orders) as that account
notes: API-based state seeding via a documented account, protocol/capability-rubric-v1.md Score 3 example.

mechanism: finale.resource() exposes the Challenge model as a queryable REST resource; app.post on /api/Challenges with security.denyAll() and app.use on /api/Challenges/:id with security.denyAll() block writes, leaving read-only GET access to each challenge's solved boolean and metadata
expected_behavior: GET /api/Challenges (or /api/Challenges/:id) deterministically reports solved true for a given challenge exactly when its documented vulnerability condition (SUT05-EV-0010, SUT05-EV-0011) has actually been triggered, and solved false otherwise
notes: Gives the API modality a source-verified, machine-readable ground-truth read-out; also supports Observability (cross-cutting).

mechanism: 61 distinct Express route modules implement first-class REST resources beyond the deterministic-account mechanism: basket, basketItems, address, orderHistory, coupon, delivery, 2fa, wallet, deliveries, createProductReviews, dataExport, dataErasure, and others (counted directly from the routes/ directory listing)
expected_behavior: Each resource is reachable and returns structured JSON, but most of these resources (unlike login/Challenges above) carry no individually documented ground-truth condition of their own
notes: Supports API breadth generally (Score 2 or higher baseline) and the Functional Complexity cross-cutting description.

mechanism: package.json description states it is probably the most modern and sophisticated insecure web application; keywords include vulnerable, pentest, capture the flag; README.md states the app encompasses vulnerabilities from the entire OWASP Top Ten along with many other security flaws found in real-world applications
notes: Documents the ecosystem's stated purpose prior to source verification.

mechanism: A catalog of 113 individually named, keyed challenges (counted directly) spanning 16 documented categories (Sensitive Data Exposure, Injection, Improper Input Validation, Broken Access Control, XSS, Vulnerable Components, Broken Authentication, Miscellaneous, Security Misconfiguration, Cryptographic Issues, Observability Failures, Broken Anti Automation, Security through Obscurity, Insecure Deserialization, XXE, Unvalidated Redirects); each entry has a description naming the specific intentional vulnerability/exploitation goal, a difficulty, hints, and a mitigationUrl
expected_behavior: Each challenge's description field is itself the defined, pre-registered expected outcome of successfully exploiting that specific documented vulnerability (for example the Password Hash Leak challenge: obtain a user's password hash via a REST API endpoint)
notes: Primary ground-truth inventory for the Security Testing modality.

mechanism: solveIf(challenge, criteria) and solve() implement server-side, automated, deterministic detection: a challenge's persisted solved field flips false to true exactly when the supplied criteria() predicate (the exact exploitation condition named in the matching data/static/challenges.yml entry) evaluates true; used at 35 call sites across routes/ (grep count, this audit)
expected_behavior: Triggering the documented vulnerability condition for a given challenge (SUT05-EV-0010) causes challenge.solved to become observably true (via SUT05-EV-0007's GET /api/Challenges and the in-app score board/notification), independent of how the condition was reached; the condition remains false otherwise
notes: Confirms the mechanism half of the Score 3 decision-procedure question for Security Testing (establish a known condition and observe a defined expected outcome).

mechanism: Some individual challenge entries carry a disabledEnv field (for example Docker and Heroku on the API-only XSS / restfulXssChallenge entry) that disables that specific challenge's solve condition under named deployment environments
notes: Limitation: the Security Testing ground-truth inventory is not perfectly uniform across every deployment environment for every individual challenge; see limitations.md. Does not change the modality-level Score 3 determination, which rests on the catalog and detection mechanism as a whole (SUT05-EV-0010, SUT05-EV-0011).

mechanism: Lists locale entries (key, icons, shortKey, display lang name) intended for selection in the UI's language switcher; 45 corresponding locale JSON translation files were counted directly under frontend/src/assets/i18n/
notes: Establishes the locale surface prior to source verification.

mechanism: this.translate.use(langKey), using Angular ngx-translate, performs an explicit, user-invokable runtime locale switch, backed by 45 shipped per-locale JSON translation files
expected_behavior: Selecting a given langKey deterministically re-renders the UI's translatable strings using that locale's shipped JSON file content, which is fixed and known in advance from the file itself in the evaluated version
notes: Explicit market/locale selection, protocol/capability-rubric-v1.md Score 3 example; mechanism and outcome both confirmed in source.

mechanism: Backend endpoint computes, per locale, a translation-completeness percentage by diffing each shipped locale JSON file against the English baseline (frontend and, where present, backend translation files)
notes: Supports Observability: an API-observable, source-verified measure of translation completeness per locale.

mechanism: Searched the full 113-entry challenge catalog's 16 documented categories, all 61 route modules, and all 14 config profiles for a Performance/load/Denial-of-Service/rate-limit category, challenge, or configuration toggle describing an intentional, controllable performance-degradation condition
expected_behavior: A documented category, challenge entry, or config toggle describing such a condition, with a defined measurable expected outcome (e.g. an expected latency or throughput change), would have been observed
notes: Negative evidence for the Performance modality: none found.

mechanism: The 61 REST route modules and the Express server they attach to are reachable by a generic HTTP load-testing tool (for example k6 or Artillery) exactly as contemplated by protocol/capability-rubric-v1.md Score 1's definition
expected_behavior: The evaluated version itself provides no specific performance ground truth beyond generic reachability (see SUT05-EV-0016)
notes: Supports Score 1 for Performance.

file_path_or_endpoint: package.json (dependencies and devDependencies, full file read)
mechanism: Searched package.json's full dependency and devDependency lists for an accessibility-testing tool (axe-core, pa11y, lighthouse, or equivalent)
expected_behavior: Presence of such a dependency, indicating the evaluated version ships or documents an accessibility-testing affordance, would have been observed
notes: Negative evidence for Accessibility — Web only: none found.

mechanism: Searched the challenge catalog's 16 documented categories (SUT05-EV-0010) and the Angular frontend application directory for any documented/labeled accessibility violation, ARIA-live test fixture, or accessibility-specific challenge entry
expected_behavior: A documented accessibility condition (for example a known missing-alt-text or contrast fault) with a defined, scanner-detectable expected outcome would have been observed; none was found. The evaluated version's Angular Material web UI (surface CONFIRMED, section 2) remains reachable by a generic accessibility scanner (e.g. axe-core) exactly as contemplated by Score 1
notes: Supports Score 1 for Accessibility — Web only. The web surface itself exists (audit.md section 2), so Decision procedure step 1 (protocol/capability-rubric-v1.md) answers yes and Score 0 does not apply.

file_path_or_endpoint: frontend/src/app (searched for a runtime theme/dark-mode toggle); config/*.yml (14 files)
mechanism: Searched the Angular frontend for a runtime (in-session) visual-condition toggle (e.g. a dark-mode switch) and the 14 config/*.yml branding profiles (7ms.yml, addo.yml, bodgeit.yml, ctf.yml, defcon33.yml, fbctf.yml, juicebox.yml, mozilla.yml, oss.yml, quiet.yml, test.yml, tutorial.yml, unsafe.yml, default.yml) for any documented, in-session-activatable visual condition
expected_behavior: A runtime-switchable visual condition with a defined expected screenshot-diff outcome would have been observed; none was found. The config/*.yml branding profiles are selected only at application startup (via NODE_ENV/config file selection), not activatable within a running session, so they do not meet the evaluated-version-already-exposes-it bar for an in-session experimental condition; the evaluated version's rendered UI remains reachable by a generic screenshot-diff tool (e.g. Pixelmatch) exactly as contemplated by Score 1
notes: Supports Score 1 for Visual Testing.

expected_behavior: An Android build directory/project or a cross-platform mobile framework dependency would have been observed; none was found. The evaluated repository is a single Node.js/Angular web application (frontend/, routes/, server.ts)

expected_behavior: An iOS build directory/project or a cross-platform mobile framework dependency would have been observed; none was found
structural_scope_note: NO_MOBILE_SURFACE: no iOS application build exists in the evaluated version (juice-shop/juice-shop at commit 1618a611b173b4bf114028e6e02549950606e29d)

mechanism: captchas() generates a math CAPTCHA using Math.random() for three operands and two operators on every request
expected_behavior: Each CAPTCHA challenge/response pair is unpredictable per request; this is stochastic behavior, not deterministic, and is distinct from the deterministic mechanisms in SUT05-EV-0002, SUT05-EV-0006, SUT05-EV-0011, SUT05-EV-0014
notes: Supports the Determinism cross-cutting property description (stochastic category).

mechanism: authorize() signs JWTs with expiresIn set to 6h
expected_behavior: A previously-established authenticated session/state (SUT05-EV-0006) becomes invalid purely due to elapsed time (6 hours) rather than any user action; this is time-dependent behavior
notes: Supports the Determinism cross-cutting property description (time-dependent category).

mechanism: The chatbot route imports createOpenAICompatible and reads the LLM_API_KEY environment variable, calling an external LLM-compatible API for chatbot responses; README.md states some challenges require an AI/LLM provider to work properly
expected_behavior: The chatbot feature's behavior and availability depend on an external service and locally-configured credentials outside the evaluated version's own control; this is external-dependency behavior
notes: Supports the Determinism cross-cutting property description (external-dependency category); also a limitation (feature requires external configuration to fully exercise).

mechanism: First-party Cypress end-to-end tests target the login form via stable static id selectors (email, password, loginButton) and use a custom cy.expectChallengeSolved() command tied to the SUT05-EV-0007/SUT05-EV-0011 challenge-state mechanism; 32 Cypress e2e spec files and 57 API test files were counted directly under test/cypress/e2e/ and test/api/
expected_behavior: Stable, documented selectors and a first-party automation harness exist in the evaluated version
notes: Supports the Automation Affordances cross-cutting property description. Sampled from one spec file among 32; not exhaustively verified across every screen (see limitations.md).

mechanism: 23 Sequelize model files define the evaluated version's data entities: address, basket, basketitem, captcha, card, challenge, challengeDependency, complaint, delivery, feedback, hint, imageCaptcha, memory, privacyRequests, product, quantity, recycle, securityAnswer, securityQuestion, user, wallet (plus index and relations modules)
notes: Supports the Functional Complexity cross-cutting property description (entity inventory).

mechanism: Searched routes/ and server.ts for an endpoint or handler implementing a full application-state reset (distinct from the per-user password-reset flow); a search for reset across routes/ and server.ts matched only routes/resetPassword.ts
expected_behavior: An HTTP-triggerable full-state reset endpoint, if it existed, would have been found among the 61 route modules
notes: Supports the Resetability cross-cutting property description: no in-session/API reset endpoint found; the only reset mechanism identified is the process-restart-triggered reseed (SUT05-EV-0003).

mechanism: GET /metrics serves Prometheus-format runtime metrics via register.metrics(), and GET /rest/admin/application-version reports the running application version; server.ts's own inline comment marks the /metrics exposure as the deliberate exposedMetricsChallenge
expected_behavior: Both endpoints return structured, inspectable diagnostic data without requiring authentication, in the evaluated version
notes: Supports the Observability cross-cutting property description (diagnostic endpoints); the /metrics exposure is itself one of the SUT05-EV-0010 challenge catalog entries.
